articleTitle: VRLA batteries in photovoltaic energy storage systems for telecom applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The Swiss PTT has installed an active repeater station powered by a photovoltaic energy storage system (PVES) on the peak Pit Muttler situated in the vicinity of the border corner Switzerland-Austria-Italy at an altitude of 3294 m. The PVES system consists of 72 60 W (4.32 kW-36m/sup 2/) solar panels with associated maximum power trackers and charging controllers. The photovoltaic energy is stored in 24 V batteries using 2 V VRLA Compact Power cells with a nominal capacity of 1000 Ah (C/sub 10/) per cell. In order to evaluate the worst case conditions of extremely low temperatures within the battery room, the low temperature (-30/spl deg/C) and the low voltage (0.00 V/cell) behaviour of such cells is reported. Batteries survive freeze/thaw cycles unscathed and can be recharged with the electrolyte "frozen".<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safeguard and renovation of air conditioning installations for communication centers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The rooms in which communication centers are set up must be kept in clean air, temperature and hygrometry conditions compatible with building recommendations. Here, the author discusses the following requirements for communication center air conditioning installations: nonstop working of the machines; a temporary solution in case of a failure or renovation works; two backup products, heavy and light; restraint for the building; electric power and air ducts setting; area access; hot air extraction; operation; and maintenance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Active clamp PWM forward converter with self driven synchronous rectification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The necessity of developing high efficiency and high power density on board DC/DC power converters with low output voltage for telecommunication applications leads to substitution of the rectifier diodes of the output stage by synchronous rectifiers. Control complexity and driving losses are the main constraints of this technique. A very simple implementation of self driven synchronous rectification in the active clamp PWM forward power converter is proposed. The absence of control circuitry and the minimization of losses are the main benefits of this circuit, whose analysis and optimization are addressed. Very high overall efficiency (89%) has been obtained in an actual prototype (3.3 V, 20 A).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The charge equalizer-a new system to extend battery lifetime in photovoltaic systems, UPS and electric vehicles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Investigations of battery banks in photovoltaic systems, UPS and electric vehicles show that individualization of single cells due to different properties leads to premature failures of the whole battery. Single cell monitoring is no way to overcome this problem. The new "charge equalizer" (CHEQ) introduced in this paper keeps all cells in the same state of charge at all times by transferring energy between the cells. For different applications, specially suited implementations of this fundamental principle are shown. The main advantages of the CHEQ will be: protection against overcharging and deep discharging of individual cells, extension of lifetime, decrease of maintenance costs, availability of the full nominal capacity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high density 48 V 200 A rectifier with power factor correction-an engineering overview
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In telecommunications installations it is desirable for power equipment to draw a balanced three phase current at unity power factor with zero neutral current. A compact 48 V, 200 A rectifier weighing 32 kg has been commercially developed for this need. The rectifier employs the power conversion techniques first reported at INTELEC 1989 by Dennis Chapman of Swichtec Power Systems (formerly Eltec Electronics), New Zealand. Powered from a three wire, three phase 400 V, 50-60 Hz supply the rectifier presents essentially a unity power factor to the line. The thermal layout adopted, combined with fan cooling, keeps the overall dimensions to 400 mm wide/spl times/178 mm high/spl times/460 mm deep (4U/spl times/19 inch rack module). Maximum continuous output power is 11.2 kW (56 V, 200 A) at an efficiency of 90%. The rectifier comprises three modules. Each module operates at 230 V AC and can supply up to 70 A at 56 V DC. The three modules are connected in a star or 'Y' configuration. The junction point of the three modules is maintained at the equivalent neutral point voltage by controlling the power processed by each module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detection of faults of filter capacitors in a converter. Application to predictive maintenance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: One of the most frequent reasons of breakdown of static power converters, and in particular switch mode power supplies, is the failure of filter electrolytic capacitors. With the use of time-worn capacitors, or by modelling the faults artificially, the authors have developed a fault indicator. By comparing the latter with data representing the system during normal running, they have achieved an estimate of imminent failure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuse model for over-current protection simulation of DC distribution systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The design and analysis of overcurrent protection for telecommunication DC power systems can be greatly assisted by the use of a computer-aided simulation tool. This paper reports on the development of a fuse model for SPICE derived software that can accurately represent characteristic fuse parameters. The fuse model can also be adapted to represent the operation of circuit breakers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic current shaper with fast output regulation and soft-switching
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new utility-to-DC, harmonic-free interface combines the functions of automatic input current shaping, fast output voltage regulation, and lossless, soft switching in a single power converter. This was made possible through internal energy storage and the discovery of new modes of operation, which together, effectively decoupled the input boost-like part of the Cuk converter from its buck-like output. Experimental results obtained on a 50 W-12 V prototype confirm the fast output regulation (30 kHz bandwidth for 100 kHz switching frequency) simultaneously with low-harmonic line current waveforms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved variable capacitance device and its applications to resonant converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new variable capacitance device for use in power electronics is proposed. The capacitance of this device can be varied by DC control voltage. In the new device, constructed by ceramic capacitors, four well-balanced capacitors are bridge-connected. Therefore, the AC leakage current which flows from the control voltage terminals becomes extremely small. The series resistance for suppressing the leakage current can be removed unlike the former three-terminal device. This brings a marked decrease in the time constant as seen from the control voltage terminals. The transient response times are investigated in the case when this device is used as the resonant capacitor of resonant power converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Very high efficiency techniques and their selective application to the design of a 70 A rectifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Latest techniques for the design and construction of high efficiency, high performance switched mode power supplies are investigated, compared with older techniques, and implemented in the optimised design of a 70 A, 54 VDC telecommunications rectifier which draws unity power factor from the AC supply while exceeding 93% conversion efficiency. A new 'lossless' snubber is introduced which combines di/dt and dv/dt limiting properties to greatly improve efficiency while using 30% fewer parts than conventional 'lossy' snubbers. Another novel approach used is the parallel combination of IGBT and MOSFET to form a hybrid power switch with a very low on-voltage and a low turn-off loss. Contrary to popular trends the switching frequency is kept low to minimise switching losses. The combination of these techniques and others discussed in the paper, yields a unit with excellent efficiency and some advantages which further benefit both manufacturer and end user.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High frequency ZVS for high power rectifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a family of rectifiers with power outputs from 1.5 kW to 7 kW, based on high frequency (200 kHz) converters using power MOSFETs. The circuit uses full-bridge converters in the quasi-resonant mode (zero-voltage switching), which results in very low switching losses. Both single-phase and three-phase designs are available. The single-phase 230 V versions are equipped with a power factor controller to comply with IEC 555-2. Two bridges are mounted in series for operation from a three-phase 400 V supply. An innovative construction of the power transformer, protected by a patent, guarantees perfect equilibrium between the two bridges without any additional control circuit. The principle is also extended to transformers mounted in parallel for higher power levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of suitable PWM topologies to meet very high efficiency requirements for on-board DC/DC converters in future telecom systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In order to meet the very high frequency requirements demanded by on-board DC/DC converters for future telecommunication systems, new rectification techniques for PWM topologies are deeply analyzed in this paper. The main objective is to improve the efficiency of the rectification stage and to keep the physical dimensions of the whole converter under established limits. Taking into account this criterion, different solutions are proposed and the most promising ones are physically implemented and measured. The result shows efficiency improvements between 5 and 7 points compared to the classical implementations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical reliability modelling of complex telecommunications services
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The design of telecommunications power and air-conditioning services is to very high levels of reliability, but when do you begin to over-capitalise in providing engineering services and how can you distinguish between two complex systems on a cost/performance basis? This paper describes the results of modelling complex telecommunications systems using a new commercially available software reliability tool. Common areas of over-capitalisation are highlighted. Field survey information is presented on the performance of AC mains and standby generators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Three-phase power factor controller with minimum output voltage distortion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A single-switch fully-controlled three-phase rectifier is presented, which provides high AC power factor and wide DC voltage regulation while allowing high-frequency insulation. Owing to one-cycle control, output voltage ripple is also eliminated. Moreover, switch voltage stress is limited by a lossless clamper circuit, resulting in safe operation and high efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Three-phase 7 kW fan cooled telecom rectifier with active power factor correction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The goal of this paper is to present a new three-phase 7 kW rectifier module, which has been recently developed for the telecommunications market. Due to forced-air cooling and active power factor correction, extremely high power density (/spl ap/320 W/l) and low weight (/spl ap/20 kg) were achieved. Implementation of the most modern zero-voltage and zero-current switching techniques combined with application of state-of-the-art power switches resulted in very high efficiency (/spl ap/0.94). This together with high power factor (/spl ap/0.96) ensures optimal operation and low running costs of the rectifier.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Variables that influence results of impedance testing for valve regulated cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper demonstrates the effects of two variables that influence measured internal cell impedance values: state-of-charge and temperature. Both influences have an inverse effect in that the internal impedance will decrease as the cell is subjected to proper float charging and/or elevated temperatures. The popularity of this test technique has been propelled since the advent of the sealed valve-regulated lead acid cell, and an understanding of the data that must be collected to correlate the findings must be attained. Data presented represents tests on valve-regulated cells of both gelled and absorbed electrolyte technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Valve-regulated lead/acid battery condition monitoring
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The float voltage characteristic of valve regulated lead/acid (VRLA) batteries is considered to see if it may be used in the longer term operational service life of a battery to verify it's condition. Monitoring systems are described that are capable of measuring and recording the basic data upon which the application of the characteristic may be assessed. Initial results are given from commissioned monitor systems, and the implications of the work to date are summarised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Elimination of input harmonic currents in 3 phase AC to DC converters: a practical approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Following an introductory assessment of today's market requirements for medium size power converters, this paper illustrates many technical issues relative to three-phase controlled rectification. The various modulation schemes are briefly described and compared in terms of their performance and implementation. The discussion extends to the main power circuits with more focus on the three-phase buck topology. Considerable attention is given to the actual power handling by the rectifier section including the often overseen topics of input filter behaviour and lightning related line surge protection. The main objective of this paper is to address the subject of controlled rectification from a practical standpoint, exposing, whenever possible, the experimental evidence generated by the recent development of a 380 VAC/12 kW three phase-power factor corrected AC/DC converter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fourth order DC-DC converters with limited duty cycle range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Twelve fourth-order PWM DC/DC power converters with limited duty cycle range are treated and a survey of important data (maximum voltage and current ratings for the elements, RMS values for the semiconductor devices and a rough approximation of the losses) of the circuits are given to help to decide whether a given topology is interesting for realization. Furthermore, idealized power converter models based on duty ratio averaging are established in which continuous operation mode and ideal devices are assumed. Finally, dimensioning equations for the inductors and the capacitors are given. The results make it possible to estimate the applicability of given power converter structures and offer sufficient material for the calculation and analysis of these circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Environmental conditions and environmental testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Equipment engineering features, such as construction and production technology are determining factors for the stability of telecommunications equipment. Internationally accepted IEC test methods are available for environmental testing, and now there are special standardized environmental classes and test programs according to the different classes for telecommunications equipment. Developed by ETSI EE1 and recommended for conformance testing. This coordination of the classes and test methods with given severities gives appropriate tools for test engineers to get acceptable proof of the products' ability to survive (transportation, storage) and to operate under specified environmental conditions, as environmental testing belongs to the type approval procedure. This paper gives an overview of the application of the environmental and equipment engineering standards, together with examples of HTC PKI requirements, type approval procedure and laboratory test results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Origin and propagation of common mode currents occurring in a bridge rectifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The aim of this paper is to investigate the generation of common mode currents in an AC/DC power converter, in particular a silicon controlled rectifier (SCR). In fact, this paper is intended to be a first step to understanding radiated electromagnetic noise emission from an SCR and to localizing its cause and place of origin. Particular attention has been paid to the conception and implementation of the experimental set-up. The main results conclude on the incidence of the operating point on the common mode current spectra, which is due to drive signal distortion owing to interaction between the drive and control unit and the power circuit. Moreover, important dependance of the spectra on power supply impedances has been observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A development of the 2 MHz clamp mode forward ZVS-MRC on-board power module for telecommunication application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In zero voltage switched multi resonant converters (ZVS MRC), the resonant circuits are widely employed in order to effectively reduce the switching losses. However, this method give rise to high voltage stress due to the resonance, which is a drawback to the practical applications. Previously, the clamp mode ZVS MRC has been proposed, based on the clamping technique, through which the voltage stress was reduced to be 2 or 3 times the input voltage of the converter. In this work, an on-board power module is developed including the design, control and hybridization with the use of the clamp mode forward ZVS MRC. This system enables one to achieve 81% efficiency for the power module with 50 W output and 2 MHz switching frequency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel ways to improve rectifier performance from power systems' reliability viewpoint
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Technical advances are of no real relevance to a user, if they cannot offer benefits which can be measured in terms of money. The countable measures are such as improvements in equipment and system reliability, in efficiency resulting in lower internal temperature, in weight and need of space as well as in lower price. However, quite often the benefits are just marginal from the users' viewpoint. The reason is the overutilization of the obtained benefits and this can, for instance, be realized in lower reliability performance, higher price, etc. The main source of uncertainty is always public power i.e. the energy flow is not perfectly continuous. It is normally the level of voltage in public power lines which determines whether the energy is available (i.e. usable) or not. The number of outages and brownouts can be substantially reduced by means of a rectifier system which has a proper amount of filtering capacity and an adaptive (i.e. load power depending) undervoltage shut down feature. There are also other topics mainly related to system reliability from the rectifier viewpoint such as output overvoltage shut down, testing of batteries by discharging, rectifier failure detection, etc. which are discussed and solutions proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance and characteristics of valve regulated lead acid batteries with a concentric square grid design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Valve regulated lead acid batteries have been gaining acceptance in the telecommunication industry as an energy source for standby power applications. Compared to the flooded battery, they have the advantages of less maintenance and a smaller footprint. In this paper, the performance and characteristics of the AT&T VR Series Battery are presented. These batteries incorporate the patented positive grid design and the use of pure lead to provide long service life. Test results are given on capacity, self discharge, cycle life and float performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new rectifier system high efficient, high dense, modular, quick to install and superior for service
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The author describes the new CEAG S90 power system, designed for all telecom applications from 100 A-3200 A (48 V-72 V), arguing that it is the right power source for phone systems, digital data transmission, base stations for cellular phones, and other telecom services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of the influence of temperature on the behavior of the VDMOS transistor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents an accurate one-dimensional device model for the simulation of power MOSFET transistors, taking into account the effects of temperature as an interactive variable during simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fixed frequency forward ZVS-MRC using a saturable core
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a fixed frequency controlled forward ZVS-MRC (zero voltage switched-multi-resonant converter) which operates with a fixed duty ratio. It differs from the conventional forward ZVS-MRC by the placement of a saturable core in the secondary side of the transformer. The proposed converter has the following advantages: (1) lower voltage stress, (2) fixed frequency and fixed duty ratio for the main switch, and (3) simple control circuit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RAMO: management network for telecommunications environment equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The RAMO network is the fundamental tool for operating the technical environment equipment of telecommunications centres which concern the power supply, cooling system, building surveillance, access control, security, EMC and electrostatic environment. It implements functions which make it possible to analyse the quality of the equipment's performance in operation, to precisely identify equipment failures to reduce their mean time to repair. The type of equipment included in this network varies depending on the size of the centre which houses it. It comprises the power supply systems, consisting of an electrical generator, an AC distribution cabinet, a conversion and power storage cabinet from the Alfatel range, catering for all power requirements from 2.5 kVA to 60 kVA, and from the Geode range for power greater than 100 kVA, together with the cooling systems and uninterruptible power supplies. The networking of all these items of equipment on an X.25 protocol using France Telecom's operating architecture comprises the RAMO network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An assessment of commercial AC power quality: a fiber-in-the-loop perspective
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: If commercial AC voltage is used by local exchange carriers (LECs) for powering fiber-in-the-loop (FITL) systems, commercial power disturbances (outages and voltage/frequency variations) would interrupt telephone service to the customer unless back-up powering is provided. This is serious because customer expectations about the reliability of telephone services are very high-in particular, customers expect to use the telephone to notify the power company that the electricity is out. This paper provides a characterization of the frequency and duration of several categories of AC power disturbances that can have an impact on fiber-in-the-loop (FITL) service availability. The results are based on Bellcore's analysis of power disturbance data collected from sites throughout the United States during the 1990-1992 time period.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced ZVS-PWM three-phase AC-DC active power converter with new high-frequency transformer-assisted quasi-resonant DC link and its implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper is mainly concerned with the advanced soft-switching PWM three phase AC-DC active power converter with a new conceptional transformer-assisted quasi-resonant DC link (TQRDCL), which has high-performance ZVS-PWM controllability. In addition, no complexity in predictive initializing resonant inductor current control under load fluctuations are discussed. The operating principle of this TQRDCL converter with active filtering function by means of time-shared instantaneous space-voltage vector control PWM strategy and its performance evaluations are illustrated using simulated results. Furthermore, the design approach of this converter is discussed herein.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Configuration and reliability of an air-conditioning system for telecommunications systems that uses the heat dissipated from fuel cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: NTT Power and Building Facilities Inc., is now developing an air conditioning system for telecommunications use that uses the heat dissipated from phosphoric acid fuel cells. The authors have investigated the reliability of the air conditioning system and have found that the reliability of such a system can be improved if either multiple absorption refrigerators are used, or if a back-up heat supply facility (burner) is installed in an absorption refrigerator. They have also found that both an exhaust heat-driven air conditioning system and an electrically driven distributed air conditioning system must be combined to meet the reliability level required of air conditioning for telecommunications systems. In such a configuration, the number of air conditioners in the electrically driven distributed air conditioning system can be reduced by 30%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alarm communications for a FITL system remote power source
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Bellcore has worked with its clients to define a cost-effective solution for providing an alarm capability for centralized power sources not co-located with host digital terminals (HDTs). This capability considered several constraints (simplicity, economics, and mix-and-match capability). After evaluating several possible methods, it was proposed that a remote centralized power source should communicate alarms to the "closest" optical network unit (ONU) of a fibre in the loop (FITL) system. The ONU should detect alarms and the FITL system should interpret and report these alarms to an OS using its operations communications channels. In order to allow for mix and match between the FITL system and the centralized power source, an open interface was defined and alarms were grouped into three categories: commercial AC power failure (with battery back-up operating properly), major power equipment failure, and minor power equipment failure. This paper summarizes the work that was done for providing an alarm capability for centralized power sources not co-located with HDTs. It presents advantages and disadvantages of all methods considered and then describes the proposed method in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed power-a solution for the 90s
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The telecommunication industry has witnessed several major technological changes within the system equipment, architectures and the operating topologies. For power equipment vendors however, it is only with the trend towards network decentralization that system or equipment changes have triggered interest for different approaches to powering. This paper presents a distributed power plant (DPP) architecture which can be deployed effectively in both central and remote offices, in either large or small configurations. The system architecture, the market requirements, the issues of cost and space savings, the considerations for reliability and safety are all discussed and evaluated in comparison to the more traditional centralized power plant approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple output DC/DC zero-current switch quasi-resonant converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Nowadays, launched electronic equipment need more and more energy which means a bigger volume of their power supplies, leading to more expense and more EMI generation. In order to reduce these constraints, new switchmode power supply principles have been proposed, using resonance in particular. But this concept is not well adapted to multi-output power supplies. This paper shows, within an industrial feasibility project, the problems inherent to the PWM technique and proposes a simple manufacturable structure of a DC-DC multi-output power converter, with a resonant main output rated (5 V/6 A) and two secondary outputs rated (/spl plusmn/15 V/1 A) of forward type. This half-bridge structure is zero current switched with a resonant frequency of 750 kHz. The bidirectional secondary current is consumed by synchronous rectifiers. Moreover this solution gives good efficiency even at low loads which is essential in such equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of the physical and electrical phenomena in different surge-protective circuits for low-voltage AC power line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Surge protective circuits for low-voltage AC power line are made up with nonlinear passive components, such as gas tube arresters, gaps, varistors (ZnO, SiC) and diodes. Being very different from the electrical characteristics, the advantages and drawbacks of such surge suppressors depend mainly on the type of components used and the possibility of combining them with one another. Based on the study of the degradation of the components under surge current stress, the physical and electrical phenomena in different surge protective circuits have been discussed in this paper. The authors therefore present a comparison of the essential differences in two surge protective circuits on the French market.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Valve regulated gel-batteries for stand-by-applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Valve regulated Pb-acid batteries for standby power application are known today in two technologies, the gel and the AGM system. Both systems are distinguished from conventional batteries by the use of solid electrolytes, to enable oxygen recombination. Because gel batteries have a lower recombination rate than AGM types, float current and heat generation of gel cells is also lower than that for AGM cells. According to the low float current, overheating up to thermal runaway is not noticed at gel batteries in float applications. Properties of industrial gel batteries in gas extrication and float life are discussed. A strong demand of the user is the possibility to recognize the state of age of valve regulated batteries without discharging, which cannot be solved at the moment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field test on a fuel cell energy system for telecommunications equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: At two telephone offices in Japan, the authors are field testing a fuel cell energy system in which electric and heat energy is fed to the telecommunications equipment and air conditioning system. The test is expected to confirm the usefulness of the interface between the fuel cell energy system and telecommunications power feeding, air-conditioning system and demonstrate the reliability, maintenance and operation of the fuel cell system. This paper explains the background and the system configuration, and it presents the interim findings of the field test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-step high-ohmic distribution system: a distribution system in which each printed board assembly is a disablement unit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The dimensions of telecommunication equipment are diminishing and there is a growing demand for using single printed board assemblies as disablement units. This paper presents a solution fulfilling this demand while still limiting the number of distribution cables to one or a few in each subrack. A comparison with other theoretical solutions is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new supervisioned telecom power plant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Working from specifications supplied by SIP, ITALTEL have designed and developed a new series of 48/60 V medium and high power power plant, that can be connected to a supervision and control network whose monitoring capabilities can be extended down to the level of a single rectifier. This infrastructure is arrived at by choosing a system architecture in which the connection between supervision network and control device of the power distribution system is achieved via a serial port to port link; this device is then connected to control devices on each rectifier via a multiport serial connection. The system architecture is described in this paper, along with the characteristics of the new power plant, with particular emphasis on the remote management capabilities, and the control devices that have made the implementation possible. Particular attention has been placed on the battery management, developing algorithms that include a test to allow local and remote control of functionality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compact, high-efficiency, high-power DC/DC converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A 10 kW (53 V/200 A), forced-air-cooled DC-DC power converter has been developed for fuel cell systems. This converter uses a new HV bipolar-mode static induction transistor (BSIT), a new driving method, a ZVS PWM technique and a new litz wire with low AC resistance. It weights only 16.5 kg, has a volume of 26,000 cm/sup 3/, operates at 40 kHz and has a power conversion efficiency of about 95%. The power loss of this converter been reduced by 20% with respect to a conventional natural-air-cooled DC-DC converter for a power density 3 times superior.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and design of multiple-output converters with stacked secondaries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Stacking secondaries or outputs is an effective way to improve DC cross-regulation for multiple-output power converters. In this paper, various stacking schemes are presented, and DC analysis is performed for each particular scheme. The analysis reveals that stacking introduces an internal voltage compensation mechanism which provides output voltage tracking as any load current changes. The effects of stacking on power loss and current stress of the rectifiers are also analyzed. The analyses are verified on an experimental two-output forward power converter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supercapacitors for telecommunication applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Supercapacitors are electrochemical energy storage devices that can find several applications in the power systems for telecommunications. The principle of these components is explained and their relative characteristics are described. Different applications are envisioned in the stationary and portable areas. Their use would allow the realization of more reliable uninterruptible power supplies and higher performance power sources for portable telecommunications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New testing methods for evaluation of the life of lead/acid batteries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Previously defined methods of evaluating the life of lead-acid batteries do not permit the establishment of a reliable relationship between laboratory test data and the service life of batteries in actual use. As a result, it has been necessary to define alternative nondestructive methods of test which can be accurately correlated with life. For this, the method consists of an elevated temperature test at a constant float voltage. Capacity measurement at defined time intervals, and an assessment of the degree of grid corrosion which is compared to the corrosion behaviour of cells with known periods on float at room temperature. The correlation factor between the test and actual service can therefore be precisely assessed. Earlier test methods are outlined and the procedure for the new test is described. Results are given for the life of various types of battery in standby power applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A bonding topology for new communication equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents the findings of many studies conducted over the past few years to evaluate viable alternatives that could be used as a grounding strategy for new communication equipment utilizing high frequencies, distributed architecture and a variety of existing communication links. A system built in accordance with the proposed architectures would be suitable for installation in accordance with different national standards, operating company practices and grounding topologies without redesign, internal changes, or circuit modifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Valve-regulated lead/acid batteries for telecommunications service
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The widespread use of valve regulated lead/acid (VRLA) batteries for telecommunications service has resulted in high levels of reliability and reduced operating costs. The development of VRLA batteries to meet critical requirements for both large and small applications is described. The range of sealed lead/acid batteries has been extended to larger capacities using both absorptive glass mat and gel technologies. For smaller batteries, better efficiency and durability is being achieved with cells using pure lead grids. These approaches are discussed and future directions for the further development of VRLA batteries for telecommunications are indicated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Setting a uniform interface for energy-network management. An implementation study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The introduction of a telecommunications network management system is a process extended over a long period of time. All long term plans are based on forecasts. These forecasts in turn are based on experience of previous development. Because of rapid technological development in the field of network management together with increasing demands for cost effective operation of the telecommunications network, the need for development and introduction of a network management system with standardized interfaces for energy supply equipment is urgent. With the rapid development taking place in the telecommunications area today, it is of importance that previous decisions/plans do not interfere with future plans. This paper describes how the Swedish Telecommunications Administration has, since 1984, worked at the introduction of automatic supervision of energy supply equipment, retaining flexibility for the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Revolution within UPS systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: With recent innovations, it has been possible to make a generation of online uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) without some of the disadvantages of traditional systems. These new systems utilize a single conversion technology which gives very high efficiency and no mains repercussions. The authors describe DATAPOWER systems, the newest member of which has achieved an efficiency of 96% for a 3 kVA UPS system. The DATAPOWER family are manufactured by Silicon, and are available from 500 W to 2 MW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new era has begun in Japan's telecommunications energy systems' operations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: On December 1, 1992, a new company, NTT Power and Building Facilities Inc., was established. This started a new era in Japan's telecommunications energy systems' operations. Engineering and management activities for telecommunications energy systems and buildings that Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation (NTT) had previously conducted within its organization were transferred to the new company in the form of a specialized business. This new company is the first instance in which NTT has organized its existing activities as a full-scale business, and the move is significant from the standpoint of managerial promotion in the NTT group. Here we discuss the circumstances that led up to this commercialization and the fundamental purpose reflected by its goals and status.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decentralized, intelligent DC power plant communicates with the switching system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The author describes SIMPS (system integrated modular power supply), a decentralized power supply predominantly designed for the switching system ALCATEL 1000 S12 in its method of construction of the "J"-rack family, falling in line with the racks of a telephone exchange. The signalling scheme is very closely adjusted to the feasibility and recommendations of this system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A flexible distributed solution for energy management in telecommunications networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The paper describes the Alenia solution to the telecommunication network operators problem of the energy stations' cost effective maintenance. Due to the different technologies employed in energy station equipment the Alenia system performs remote monitoring, diagnosis and control of energy stations in a telecommunication network in a way that is homogeneous and independent from the type and the technology of the controlled equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A three-phase rectifier with reduced pollution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Considering their input behaviour, diode rectifiers are nonlinear loads that disturb the mains because of harmonic currents and high peak currents values. European standards have been published and limit the pollution for any single-phase customer. These standards will soon be generalized to the three-phase network. This is the reason why the authors wanted to prove the feasibility of an IGBT rectifier with unity power factor. The output power of this prototype reaches more than 2O kW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A voltage type PWM rectifier with instantaneous current control capability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new control strategy for a three phase voltage type PWM rectifier is described. This control strategy introduces state feedback control of an LC filter inserted on the AC side of the power converter and has the advantage of fast response to changes in the input current and in the load while operating with unity power factor and sinusoidal AC supply currents to produce a regulated DC voltage. Simulation results from a study of the PWM rectifier with the proposed control strategy show that the transient performance is improved and the supply current follows closely the reference current even for very low resistance of AC side inductors. Experimental results are also included to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Video dial tone powering issues
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The principal objective of the power architectures described in this paper is to provide adequate electrical power and reserve power, as needed, to network-owned Video Dial Tone (VDT) electronics. This paper discusses the main advantages and disadvantages of important powering strategies and their life-cycle costs. Life-cycle costs show that locally provided power without an AC interface unit and battery backup, or customer-provided powering of VDT electronics are cost-effective powering strategies compared to network-provided power and backup. The paper also identifies potential road-blocks that need to be addressed in order to facilitate the timely and cost-effective deployment of VDT services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Zero-voltage soft-switching discrete pulse modulated three-phase AC-DC power converter with an active filtering function and its extended application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art discrete pulse modulated (DPM) three-phase AC/DC power converter with an active-voltage clamped resonant DC link (ACRDCL). Its DSP-based digital control strategy to realize unity power factor correction and sinewave line current shaping is proposed. The operating characteristics are illustrated using simulation results and experimental data. In addition, the bidirectional double power conversion circuit with a single stage ACRDCL is demonstrated as an extended concept of the switched mode DPM rectifier treated here.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lightning currents coupling to metal tubes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Signal and control cables are often placed in closed metal tubes for optimal protection from induced overvoltages in case of lightning. The key parameter is the current distribution along the tube, which is closely related to the currents flowing through the earthings to which the tube is connected. A careful analysis of the current distribution has to be made prior to the coupling study. A computer model based on electromagnetic field theory, which takes into account the interactions between different parts of the conductors is described. The distribution of the current is assessed in both frequency and time domains. The influence of a shield wire placed near the tube is also analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved systems reliability through improved battery monitoring techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The standards for reliability in critical backup power systems are increasing. To meet the standards, even better batteries, better system integration of batteries, and continuous monitoring of batteries should be employed. This paper focuses on continuous monitoring of batteries. Monitoring which can increase system reliability and further improve battery life, performance, and reduce overall systems costs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical evolution of -48 V DC reserve systems reduces the need for UPS in the telecom industry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A fast growing segment of the telecommunication industry is the integration with equipment from the computer market. This type of equipment will be used by operators for providing new services throughout the telecommunication network. Sparked by the growing use of such "service providing equipment", the use of existing -48 V DC reserve systems will be more widely spread, and reduces the need of conventional UPS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The soldiese hybrid system-operation on a high altitude relay for mobile radiocommunications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: New relays have been installed in France in response to the development of radiocommunications with mobile phones, and the deployment of the Itineris system (GSM) in particular. It is in this context that France Telecom has installed, at an altitude of 2600 m in the Alps, a hybrid photovoltaic/diesel engine generator system to provide a continuous power supply of 1.5 kW. This paper sets out the solutions adopted and provides the first operating results for this station.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The air velocity problem [air conditioning]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In recent decades, the heat generated by electronic components has constantly been increasing. For equipment cooled by air, it has therefore been necessary to successively increase air velocity. This tendency is associated with many problems at the premises, cabinet and circuit board levels. Some of the problems are specific for each particular level but one problem is common for all of them, the power consumption of the fans. A condensed resume of the problems associated with high air velocities is made and some suggestions for future solutions are also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protection from lightning of France Telecom centres: from kilo-amperes to kilo-francs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This article tackles the problem of lightning protection applied at France Telecom on both economic and organizational levels. Technical principles, validated during Saint Privas d'Allier experimentation, and treated in several articles, is briefly recalled. However, from data available on the elderly running stations, the earnings linked to the bonding network and its associated devices are carefully assessed. Another subject-as far as organization is concerned-is difficulties implied by such an important cultural change as passing from the "star earthing method" to the "mesh bonding network", both within France Telecom and towards its relations with its suppliers or customers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Building control and management system for supervision and remote management of the environment telecommunications equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Air conditioning installations for telecommunications equipment must fulfil three essential requirements without breaking down: reliable high-quality service to satisfy the comfort needs and to protect the normal operation of the technical installations; permanent control of the operating costs; and maintenance services. The management systems of the Staefa control system are specifically developed for the control and remote management of technical equipment for building services. Experience and partnerships with professionals from the air conditioning sector enable Staefa to successfully apply the most advanced technical solutions to the control and management of the environment for telecommunications installations. Ideal surrounding conditions are provided to all types of technical equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer analysis of telecom battery racks resistant to earthquakes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The function of batteries is to provide the energy of telecom equipment without interruption at mains failure. Depending on battery reserve and seismic zones, telecom organizations require analysis of battery racks resistant to earthquakes according to national standards and international recommendations. This paper deals with the computer analysis of battery racks resistant to earthquakes. The analysis is based on the finite element method (FEM) with seismic motion given with design response spectrum (DRS). Finally, there is also given a graphical survey of rack vibrations for a particular DRS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Economical acquisition and use of batteries. Traditions and beliefs as a hinder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: There are many deeply rooted beliefs in the use of batteries affecting the economical acquisition and use of them. These traditions and beliefs stem mostly from the recommendations of battery manufacturers. These recommendations are often based more on the business interests of battery manufacturers then on the interests of battery users. These traditions and beliefs have cause substantial extra costs for users during the last twenty years. The persistent belief that a 20% reduction of nominal capacity means the end of useful battery life and that the reduction will certainly take place during the design life of the battery as well as that only similar (i.e. age, capacity type, manufacturer and technology) battery strings can be connected in parallel, are such beliefs which have caused these extra costs. The costs are due to resulting battery sizing and disposal practices. This paper presents the studies carried out in Finland concerning the parallel connection of different battery strings. In addition, the practical constraints of paralleling and its effect on fault detection as well as on reliability performance are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technologic plants managements with TMN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: France Telecom has developed RAMO, a tool for local and remote management of the telecommunication public network technological environment (such as power supply equipment, buildings, air conditioning, etc.). In larger sites, a local supervision system allows visualisation of alarms and operating states and acts upon network equipment. Smaller centers are managed from a remote supervision system connected via a private X25 network. Larger sites can also be managed from the remote system. RAMO is independent of the general management of public networks; maintenance, end-users management, accounting, etc. In the long term, this situation must evolve into a centralized structure managing all network management fields. The architecture is based on principles defined by the CCITT Recommendation M30 that describes the telecommunication management network (TMN). This article proposes several solutions for the integration of the RAMO tool and the technical environment within the TMN. However, considering current France Telecom tools, management rules, and economic aspects imply a low technical level solution that satisfies all other aspects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Problems of the application of new power systems in Hungarian telecom network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The development of telecommunications systems, and with them the development of necessary power equipment, has also brought new tasks for Hungarian Telecom including modernisation of the old technical requirements of the power supply as well as type approval testing of the new power systems. The PKI Telecom Institute is a participant in both tasks. In this report, the authors describe the aspects of technical requirements, the differences between the old and new systems and requirements, measurements and the activity of the PKI in these domains.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Availability control of the back-up power supply for remote terminals in an optical custom network with "FTTH" system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new system for measuring the ageing and charge condition of NiCd or NiMh batteries with remote diagnosis facilities for back-up fibre to the loop (FTTH) power supplies is described by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: More compact and lighter design of 48 V 50 A switching power supply for telecommunications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The rising number of base stations for cellular, automobile, and other mobile telephones is increasing the demand for telecommunications power supplies. Often these base stations are installed in confined spaces, because of which there are strong demands that power supplies are compact and lightweight. The described, recently developed, 48 V 50 A switching power supply unit for telecommunications has increased efficiency substantially over preexisting units through means such as an enhancement in the turnoff timing of switching elements to prevent the occurrence of surge voltage, and has in addition reduced size and weight.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PWM inverter for parallel operation as high quality AC source in telecommunication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents power conversion in an inverter without a 50 Hz transformer, delivering high quality line-type AC power drawn from a 48/60 V DC source. Two modes of operation of such inverters are known: single and double modulation. Advantages and disadvantages of both modes are presented and compared. Basing on this comparison an inverter has been developed which has distortion free AC voltage output, relatively small volume and weight and high efficiency. It uses IGBTs and MOSFETs controlled by an optimised PWM strategy. This inverter can synchronise with the mains and can be parallel connected to increase output power and system redundancy. By the use of a static bypass unit, a further increase in redundancy may be achieved. An example of application in a telecommunication power supply is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative study of various surge arrester modules for low voltage networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The paper discusses a comparative study of the performance, under permanent and transitory working conditions, of various modules for the protection of low-voltage electrical installations against overvoltages. Four types of module were studied: (i) a ZnO varistor alone; (ii) a series association of a varistor with an air gap; (iii) two varistors in series: one of which can be short-circuited by the air gap; and (iv) a combination of the first and the second in parallel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power architecture: global power for wireless, data and fiber access
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: From business definition to strategies, tactics and then down to systems' architecture and their compliance with technical specifications, everything has to be thought and next defined within a "global" frame. The subject of this paper deals with one of the many things which can be globalized in a global telecommunication network-the power. With the increase in competition between "phone" services providers and with the increase in the innumerable services which can now be supplied over the "phone" line whatever this might be: copper, fiber or air, it is imperative to properly look at the power from a new angle and define adequate, common architecture which makes it easy to implement, exploit and maintain power systems for the year 2000 and beyond. This paper analyzes the similarities and suggests a global approach for the power architecture for the newest, fastest growing access technologies: fiber, data and personal communication. The analysis is based on, and starts with existing copper access power systems for both POTS/data and CATV and uses them as the foundation on which the access power systems will be built.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Considerations in preparing a specification for stationary valve regulated lead-acid batteries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: International standards as well as draft international standards (IEC and CENELEC) and guidelines (i.e. EUROBAT) for the understanding and use of valve regulated lead-acid batteries have now been issued. Purchase of valve regulated batteries must be accompanied by a "purchasing specification". The work of preparing a specification for these batteries was undertaken on a joint basis in the Nordic countries (Scandinavia and Finland). Among the issues addressed in connection with this project were requirements relating to quality, performance, operation and the environment. A purchasing specification based on numerous reference documents, international standards and guidelines and battery manufacturers' product information has been drawn up. The paper presents some of the above-mentioned issues and aspects which have been discussed during the work of preparing the specification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: More accurate modelling of earthing systems transient behaviour
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Two computer models for analysis of transient behaviour of earthing systems based on the electromagnetic theory have been developed. The computer models are based on different mathematical models and different numerical techniques are applied. The first goal of the analysis is to compute the longitudinal current distribution in the earthing electrodes. Then once the currents are determined, other parameters of interest such as near fields, voltages, leakage currents, impedance, etc. may be determined by further calculations. In this paper the emphasis is given to computation of the induced overvoltages in circuits placed near the earthing systems in case of lightning. Comparison with the previous, more simplified computer models, shows that new models predict much greater induced transient voltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The uninterruptible battery system-UBS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the uninterruptible battery system (UBS) which was developed by Best Power Technology, Incorporated, to extend the operating reserve time of essential systems while minimizing battery plant size. Present applications include remote telecommunications facilities, computer systems, railroad signaling locations, cellular radio locations, and uninterruptible power systems (UPS). Operating experience for over 212 system-years are used to compare reliability and cost improvement with the new system over traditional techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switch room cooling-a system concept with switch room located cooling equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: To the traditional requirements of cooling systems for telecommunications switching equipment are now added, concurrently with rising energy prices and labour costs, requirements on energy and space efficiency and installation and maintenance friendliness. This paper describes a cooling system based on water, with compact units that can be placed in the same room as the equipment to be cooled by the system. The heat transport from the switching equipment to the system is based on the well-tried principle of natural convection. The central points of this paper are the switch room cooling concept, the principle of natural convection and the energy saving free cooling function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Air flow measurements inside the switching center of France Telecom at Eurodisney
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: CETIAT carried out flow rate measurements inside the technical room of a telephone exchange fully equipped with electronic equipment. A false floor equipped with 54 air conditioning terminals takes charge of the air diffusion inside the room in order to remove the heat released by the equipment. CETIAT designed and realized a special flowmeter to measure the flow rate at each supplying terminal and another for the exhaust terminal. The first flowmeter is composed of a transformation piece, a CETIAT flowmeter and a fan compensating the pressure drop of the system and fixing the ambient pressure in the transformation piece. The results obtained at the floor and at the ceiling made it possible to determine the air flow distribution and diffusion inside this technical room.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Are telephone exchanges energy efficient? EE2000, a technique for taking the energy pulse of telephone exchanges
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for enhancing energy efficiency in telephone exchanges. These include techniques for verifying energy efficiency levels, broadly classifying exchanges according to efficiency enhancement requirements and proposing efficiency enhancement measures with the aid of energy flow analyses and energy consumption follow-ups. Although principally concerned with measurability and verification of energy efficiency levels-that is with "a technique for taking the energy pulse of telephone exchanges"-the article also includes a brief account of the project behind the methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelligent networking in power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The modern trend in telecommunications to distributed networks has led to a requirement for decentralised power systems. Intelligent networking of such power systems can help provide the necessary system integrity while maintaining reasonable costs. This paper describes some of the requirements of such an intelligent network and describes an implementation known as facilities data management. The hardware and software elements of the system are described, along with several examples of networks to suit different requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arc detection for telephone DC power distribution systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Arcing faults may occur in DC power distribution systems in telephone offices. Fuses and circuit breakers are not intended to protect against arcing faults. Therefore, the detection of arcing faults is a prime concern to help prevent fire ignition and the resulting damage caused by fire and its by-products. This paper describes a method to help detect arcing faults in telephone offices. It includes the work determining arc signatures and noise spectra in working, nonarcing, DC power distribution systems. Also, field and laboratory experiments investigating the performance of an experimental prototype arc detection system are described. Possible applications of an arc detection system are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of telecommunication systems as a function of their environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents ideas and models which do not enable the calculation of absolute values for the reliability of telecommunication network nodes, but allow an analysis of different solutions by the adoption of a uniform standard measure. The influence exercised by the various types of telephone connections with their different kinds and numbers of components can likewise be determined with the aid of these models. What is more, the models permit a relation to be established to the repair service and its organizational and technical facilities, so that it can be included in such reliability considerations. In addition, these models enable estimation of the impact of reliability on the quality of service offered to the customer. Thus they are also well-suited for solving reliability problems arising from optical fibre application in the subscriber line network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New modular and intelligent telecommunication power supply systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Under the renewal program of the Italian telecommunication network and to improve the quality of all telephone network components, SIP (the Italian operating telecommunication company) has issued new specifications for DC power supply and its remote supervision network. Under this program, optics ALCATEL ITALIA together with SIP has developed a new family of DC power supplies ranging from 12 A up to 4000 A, both for centralized and dedicated applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computerized test equipment for stationary batteries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A growing number of stationary lead-acid battery installations are reaching the limits of their service life. In order to safely extend their service life, computer based battery testing and monitoring systems have been used successfully to determine the capacity without subjecting the battery to a complete discharge, as would normally be the case in standard practice. This paper describes the technical issues surrounding the test equipment and the methodology.
