Test results from over 8000 cells are presented, along with a case study showing how the service life of an aging battery was extended by two years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ECU: universal monitoring system in management network-a new kind of philosophy in remote processing for telecommunication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: ECU is an independent and intelligent technical server for remote processing, remote maintenance of industrial infrastructure equipment, technical environments and transmission lines. Born out of France Telecom's national mission, its principal role is to be a node of communication between all independent supervision networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The analysis and design of full-bridge series-resonant type 48 V 200 A rectifier unit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents new topologies of full-bridge series-resonant type 48 V 200 A rectifier units as battery chargers for telecommunication systems. Two advantageous points of this topology are shown: one improves the reverse recovery characteristic of the anti-parallel-diode of the main switching devices; and the other improves audible noise under light load conditions. A prototype unit is realized which is 3.0 cc/W in size and 2.7 g/W in weight. Conversion efficiency is 92%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1500 W high power density rectifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This article presents the most significant choices and the problems encountered during the design and conception of a 1 MHz single phase rectifier (230 V AC/48 V DC) of 1500 W with unity power factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A truly maintenance free uninterruptible power system utilizing advance battery technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: One of the major hurdles in establishing fiber-in-the-loop (FITL) systems is the necessity of reliable power at the local level. When commercial power fails, power must be provided by a battery back-up system at the local site. Reliability and cost over the life of the battery system are critical issues that must be addressed before FITL can be implemented. They are addressed with the development of an uninterruptible power system (UPS) that utilizes advanced battery technology and an intelligent charger. The new batteries will last for over 30 years, they are more reliable than standard commercial batteries and they require no maintenance. This battery technology (which offers exceptional "fault-tolerant" provisions) allows the charge controller to acquire telemetry at all times regarding battery health and for the first time, offers a true and reliable state of charge indication, without fully discharging the battery. This paper covers basic battery and electronics design of the UPS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New high-performance static power inverter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Computers and telecommunications devices require electric power of a very high quality often provided via an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). This paper presents a new medium to high power static inverter for use in UPSs, and discusses the advantages of its high performance features in a number of fields.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supply of rectifier equipment from emergency sets-harmonic distortion and other problems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the well-known problem of disturbances, which often arise when a diesel-generator emergency set supplies a rectifier installation. The physical background of the phenomenon is explained. Analysis of current and voltage distortion is given, which permits calculations of harmonics and total harmonic distortion. A simplified theory of the synchronous machine reactances is presented, as this knowledge is necessary for the determination of voltage distortion. Experimental results are presented in order to evaluate the analytical method. The disturbances in the operation of equipment are analysed on the examples of thyristor rectifiers and phase compensation capacitors. Measures to reduce voltage distortion in the system are reviewed. The most important measures are suitable design of the emergency plant generator and resonant harmonic filters. The application of switch-mode rectifiers changes the described problem and the paper discusses to what extent the problem is alleviated. Finally, the author discusses whether or not an emergency set installation can meet the requirements of power quality standards IEC 552 and IEEE 519.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A light and compact modular 1 kW inverter with high efficiency and large input voltage range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This new, modular PWM inverter has been developed within the Eureka program with number EU202. Despite the relative complex structure that was used, the equipment consists of light, compact and high performance inverter units of 1 kW each. The paper describes the operational details of the different stages of a module, as well as the solutions used for paralleling several inverters in a reliable way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extending the reliability of DC power in a telecommunications network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: To maintain continuity of service of any telecommunications network it is necessary to provide some form of back-up power to cater for uncertainty of the public utility supply. The growing use of smaller and more remote sites associated with cellular networks and optical fibre networks really demands a compact dependable source of DC power, with minimal maintenance costs, capable of extending the back-up cover afforded by small battery installations. Engine alternator sets particularly when infrequently used and lightly loaded, often do not provide the desired level of reliability. One option that has been developed to meet this need is the aluminium-air fuel cell. Applications ranging from a few hundred watts supply required for cellular transceiver stations to a study for a 20 kW system for a major network operation are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptation of solid tantalum chip capacitors for high frequency DC-DC power supplies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In the field of power supplies, switching frequencies were previously limited to 50 or 100 kHz, therefore requiring the almost exclusive use of solid or nonsolid aluminium electrolytic capacitors for input/output filtering. The increase of these frequencies up to 500 kHz, 1 MHz or even more now allows the use of capacitors with different technologies. In this context, surface mount tantalum power capacitors, specific for this kind of application were developed. After having indicated the main characteristics of capacitors used in switching power supplies and their real operation stresses, the authors describe the technological solutions they have chosen for the manufacture of tantalum capacitors with regard to required characteristics. They present the results obtained using these capacitors submitted to usual climatic stresses and capacitors fitted in power converters after 2000 hour endurance tests. The results obtained after ripple current tests are also presented. Finally, the authors discuss the lessons learned from these investigations and the conclusions they have drawn.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New electrochemical couples to meet the requirement for mobile terminal miniaturization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The demand for uninterrupted telecommunications when commuting between home and office, by public transport, and when on holiday, has brought about an explosion in requirements for mobile equipment. In this context, the pocket terminal is becoming a universal and indispensable facility. It should be designed as a light and cheap device that everybody can carry around. The power supply is one of the main problems of miniaturization. It has to be lightweight and small with the greatest possible endurance, taking into account the typical working characteristics for this new range of products. The new electrochemical couples proposed promise eventual solutions to all these problems. The battery couples proposed are: Ni-Cd, Ni-MH, Ni-Zn, and Li ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC applied to communications spacecraft
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An artificial satellite is a bench made of a lot of electronic, electrical or electromagnetic components working in a hard environment. EMC problems encountered by communications spacecraft suppliers are reviewed. Some specific problems are a consequence of the communications mission: transmitting and receiving. As geostationary satellites, communications spacecraft have to face the difficult problem of environmental induced electrostatic discharges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photovoltaic experiences in the electric supply for relay telecommunication station in Spain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The are many reasons why Spain is considered one of the leaders in photovoltaic installations for telecommunications; plentiful sunshine, low population density, mountainous terrain and rapid economic growth during the last 20 years. This has resulted in the installation of hundreds of mountain-top relay stations. In many instances the transfer of energy via photovoltaics (PV) has proved cheaper than via the electricity grid, but because initial doubts concerning its reliability and correct functioning, this was not an argument for the installation of PV. The problems in PV are never due to the solar modules or the batteries, but always because of the sizing or of electronic parts such as control charge regulators, inverters or data collection system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System noise as a signal source for impedance measurements on battery strings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Alternating-current impedance measurements provide useful information about the characteristics of electrochemical systems, such as batteries, and are envisioned as the basis for indirect methods of determining battery capacity. Impedance measurements rely on recording the response of the battery to an applied current or voltage test signal. However, this type of measurement can be difficult with large batteries connected to operating equipment. High background noise levels, caused by time-varying changes in the battery load, interfere with the impedance measurement. Instead of attempting to eliminate background noise, the authors have used the noise as a test signal, in conjunction with Fourier transform (FT) signal processing. The current and voltage passing through cells in an operating telecommunications lead-acid battery string were determined with a simple, three-terminal connection. Impedance calculations were performed with a commercial FT signal analyzer. The results indicate that completely passive (no externally applied test signal, and not requiring discharge or disconnection of the string) impedance measurements of batteries connected to operating equipment are feasible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of the electromagnetic disturbances in the customer premises
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In order to characterize the electromagnetic environment in customer premises, CNET has started a campaign of measurement by installing nine measurement sites spread over France. Electromagnetic disturbances on telecommunications and mains components which are connected to terminal equipment are measured. The authors present the first statistical results of the peak amplitudes of the short events recorded since September 1992 to February 1993.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of air flow inside an air conditioning unit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The air conditioning system filters and regulates both temperature and humidity of the air supply to a telephone exchange. The system is comprised of a cooling unit which feeds two direct expansion V-configured finned coils. If the exchangers are to function properly, the air supply must be homogeneous, despite the apparently unfavourably assembly characteristics. Conventional velocity measurement methods are incapable of assessing this homogeneity. Two special techniques have therefore been used: laser tomography; and numerical simulation. Both investigation methods show a certain heterogeneity of the air distribution at the intake to the coils. A modified configuration was examined by digital simulation with a view to correcting the heterogeneities found in situ. The results of the study demonstrate how calculations may be used in the design and optimization of this type of installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Long duration surge transients
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Transient overvoltages or surges, generated by the most varied of causes, frequently occur in mains voltage networks. Particularly energy-rich are the surges that result when a fuse blows. Such transients have pulse widths extending into the region of milliseconds. These transients containing very high energy could damage electronic equipment. The author discusses equipment EM immunity test parameters and waveforms, the test generator and procedures, and protective measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SUNPAC: the remote monitoring of photovoltaic installations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The SUNPAC is a new device which offers a wide variety of services in order to facilitate the control, the surveillance and the remote monitoring of photovoltaic systems in remote areas. This device can be easily integrated into any PV system for isolated housing, telecommunications and water pumping. The range of power justifying the use of the SUNPAC starts from a few hundreds of Wp. By using the various capabilities that SUNPAC offers, it becomes possible to manage a range of new services, such as: user assistance for generator management; replacement of conventional measurement instruments (V, A, Ah, etc.); subsequent verification of initial system scaling; simplified scheduled maintenance; malfunction alarm prior to installation failure; and prolonged battery life.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High quality electricity by generating set
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: After a short analysis of the parameters characterizing current quality, the possibilities of standard generating sets are examined with relation to these parameters as well as the traditional solutions used to solve the problems linked with current continuity. One of the solutions that may be applied to supply good-quality continuous current, meeting the above-mentioned parameters and improving the upstream and downstream quality of the current as regards harmonics, is described in greater depth. This solution is known as the TZ set and is a combination of a dynamic uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and a diesel generating set.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arctic solar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Setting up telecom services in sparsely inhabited areas lacking even a public electricity network is generally recognised as one of the most difficult and expensive tasks a telephone company can undertake. This is especially so in Arctic areas like Finnish Lapland, where an unusually harsh environment makes exceptional demands on equipment. Here, the authors discuss how the problems of power supply have been addressed on the Finnish Telecom emergency telephone network with particular emphasis on practical experience gained in the use of solar panels and lead-acid batteries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermo-hydraulic simulation of heterogeneous equipments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Thermo-hydraulic software for electronics applications can be used to design and optimize telecommunications racks. At present, integrating multivendor devices into a single system makes it very difficult to determine thermal parameters. This study demonstrates the use of a different modelling method to handle such configurations, based on the case of a real telecommunications cabinet. This paper describes: the THEBES thermal simulation tool; the telecommunications equipment used for the study; the modelling method developed with the THEBES software; the analysis of simulation results obtained; and the advantages of that modelling method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Free standing unit utilisation, with water cooled condenser and remote dry cooler on transfer coil
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The rooms for telephone automatic switches require a precise and secure air conditioning, as well as energy consumption control. For this purpose, the following free standing air handling units (UTA) have been compared: a UTA with a remote air-cooled condenser; a UTA with a remote air-cooled condenser and free-cooling; and a UTA with a remote dry-cooler and transfer coil.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The new European telecommunication standard on earthing and bonding is a big step towards making our telecommunications more reliable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: prETS 300253 is a draft European telecommunication standard (ETS) concerning the earthing and bonding of telecommunications equipment in telecommunication centres. Standardization is a very useful way of achieving a kind of uniformity in the installation practice of equipment. The economical benefit both for the operators as well as the equipment manufacturers is clear. These considerations are well worked out in the draft-Standard itself. This contribution aims at giving a overview on the backgrounds and the scope of this draft ETS and the relation it has with CCITT recommendation K.27.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal passive systems, latent heat storage and simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The cooling storage has been considered as a new technique for use in air conditioning though the concept of this type of storage has been used for a long time in some industrial sectors. Amongst the numerous applications justifying the interest of such storage, the authors insist in particular on the function "assistance" allowed by the latent CRISTOPIA storage, which is an answer to the constant preoccupation of designers. A failure in the cooling system means a break down in production and of course a financial loss for the user. To give the cooling units the maximum safety it is usual to double the production system with an auxiliary system of the same power. Besides the high price, the use of the same type of technology for assistance and production does not mean a total reliability: the same causes often having the same effects. Therefore the "passive" technology storage function without moving mechanical parts is an opportunity. The size of assistance is established from the safekeeping period requested. This period can correspond to the intervention time required for a maintenance crew, it can extend from 1 to 5 hours.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of Petri nets to the modeling of a wind-solar power plant control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The communication protocols in multiprocessor systems give complex problems; hence it is necessary to verify the main mechanisms before setting up in order to detect eventual design errors. In this context, the use of formal description techniques is an essential aspect of the design phase. The aim of this article is to present a formal model for a real-time control system for an autonomous wind-solar power station. This model allows, on the one hand, an adequate expression of tasks to be performed (parallelism, synchronisation by message exchanges and by time constraints) and on the other, qualitative (logic of mechanisms) and quantitative (evaluation of performances) analyses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault-tolerance: reliability's reality
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In the past few years, several power-related problems have isolated large portions of the telephone network. More prudent design work might have mitigated or eliminated these failures. This paper explores several means of building fault-tolerance into the telecommunication network power plant. Also included are ideas for portable equipment which can be connected to the power bus quickly and cheaply to provide a safe work-around while maintenance activities are performed. Accordingly, a fault in the equipment being serviced is less likely to affect the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC aspects on grounding networks and DC power distribution in telecommunication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The possibility of creating galvanic isolation between two systems connected by means of coaxial cables while at the same time complying with the requirements on radiated emission from the signals on the coaxial cables, are discussed. Approximate requirements for transfer impedance for different signal speeds are also given. Induced noise voltages on shielded signal cables and internal connections inside shielded cabinets due to lightning strikes are discussed considering an isolated bonding network (IBN) with single-point connection to the common bonding network (CBN) and mesh-bonding network (MBN). The power feeding of cabinet and the filtering necessary to comply with the EMC requirements are discussed and a comparison of the filter arrangement for isolated DC return with unisolated DC return is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of technology evolution on the future of telecommunications energy management
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper, the authors visualize the telecommunications energy management systems of the next century. In particular, they propose ways in which the key areas of engineering, installation, monitoring, diagnosis and maintainance of energy/power systems of the future will be impacted by advances in computing, networking and telecommunications technologies. They review the present technologies including microprocessor control, remote monitoring, voice response, multilingual programming and networking as indicators of what the future holds. They then consider the capabilities in sophisticated user interfaces, wireless networking, increased portability and augmented system intelligence and what they portend for future energy systems products.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hydrogen sulfide and sulfur dioxide evolution from a valve-regulated lead-acid battery
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Two incidents concerning copper contamination associated with uninterruptible power systems (UPS) were observed. Valve regulated lead-acid (VRLA) batteries used in the UPSs for back-up powering were diagnosed as the possible source of the contamination. One of the VRLA batteries from the damaged UPS unit was subjected to overcharge in the laboratory, to simulate the incident. Overcharge currents greater than 10 amperes, coupled with battery temperatures over 60/spl deg/C, can cause a VRLA battery to release significant amounts of hydrogen sulfide and sulfur dioxide. Under extreme conditions, hazardous levels of hydrogen sulfide could be generated. The authors conclude that the contamination was due to copper sulfide, Cu/sub 2/S, and copper oxide, Cu/sub 2/O, formed on copper surfaces as a consequence of hydrogen sulfide evolution and the high humidity inside the UPS enclosure resulting from battery venting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quality assurance to have full control of energy systems and guarantee advanced quality
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper introduces the implementation of a quality assurance plan for the installation phase, guaranteeing quality control of energy systems used in telecommunication. Quality assurance is both a round tool in controlling product or service costs, and a way to create customer-supplier synergy based an confidence. All pre-established actions allow one to control the energy quality, all along the process of production and installation Significant results have already been obtained. Tomorrow's quality will progress due to this experience in order to focus on the optimum quality of service expected by the end user.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: End-of-charge and discharge criterion for batteries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In stand-alone photovoltaic power systems, batteries are subjected to very irregular charge-discharge patterns. Since battery voltage depends on battery current as well as on the state-of-charge, the actual battery state is difficult to determine. This paper describes a method for preventing overcharge or overdischarge by monitoring both battery current and voltage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New power feeding equipment for optical fiber submarine cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Submarine cable power feeding equipment (PFE) are direct current power supply systems, whose availability has to be very high due to the permanent service they have to fulfil. Tests and maintenance of all PFE devices, redundant power modules or system protections, are possible without any service interruption. The system complies with all EMC requirements. To achieve such purposes, we designed a modular switch mode power supply system, using numerical communication techniques with optical fibers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a 500 W/1 MHz resonant power supply
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a study of a DC-DC power supply which employs a resonant topology operating at high frequency (in MHz) in order to improve the reliability and to reduce the size of the finished product. ESE and SAFT worked together to set up the 100 W/1 MHz power supply which was financed by FRANCE TELECOM. It is a forward type power supply with voltage multi-resonance. The study was extended in order to develop a 500 W/1 MHz power supply. The authors therefore made various choices regarding the structure, the type of resonance and the components used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SvSig92-a new remote monitoring system for central power plants
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: German Telecom use central telecom power plants from many different manufacturers. There was the need for one remote monitoring system which can supervise all these different systems. Basic considerations about the different strategies of data transfer are given. It was necessary to use a low level character set to maintain compatibility of the different systems. A description of the remote monitoring system called SvSig92 is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advantages and features using a common and external error amplifier with voltage reference controlled by microcontroller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The authors describe how, in order to solve the current sharing problem in a telecommunications power system based on modular rectifiers, without the use of any additional electronics, whilst at the same time using a standard method to control the current that feeds the load and the battery, Alcatel Standard Electrica has implemented and developed a rectifier control scheme based on the use of a common and external error amplifier with a voltage reference controlled by a microcontroller for use in their intelligent power systems. This paper describes the main characteristics, advantages and features of this method, emphasizing those points needed to acquire precise management of batteries and energy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A resonant DC link inverter with low-noise and high-output power
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A resonant DC link inverter that provides high efficiency with low noise for uninterruptible power supplies has been developed. This paper describes the noise radiation, efficiency, and output voltage characteristics of a prototype resonant DC link inverter. It has 300 V DC input, and 200 V (1/spl phi/) and 10 kVA AC output. The noise radiation level meets the CISPR Pub. 22 standard and its efficiency and output voltage characteristics make it usable for practical applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage coupling using powerMOS transistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Telecommunication systems are becoming more and more compact and reliable. These requirements also apply to power converters. Reliability and compactness require an improvement in conversion efficiency and sometimes voltage distribution redundancy. This redundancy is typically performed by an "OR-ing diodes", at considerable energy loss. To correct this problem, coupling diodes can be replaced by a low Rdson powerMOS that are saturated and associated with control electronics that blocks them if there is a fault. The authors first examine the circuitry associated with these techniques. Then, they discuss the choice of components and their capacities, and finally they consider their advantages and disadvantages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new UPS for digital telecommunications systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Digital telecommunications systems are being deployed rapidly in Japan to provide various telecommunications services including basic ISDN. To control and manage these systems small computers are used that need an uninterruptible supply of AC power. To meet this need the authors have developed a new uninterruptible power supply (UPS) having the design goals of reduced installation space, enhanced electrical characteristics and lower overall cost. This paper describes the configuration, features and electrical characteristics of the new UPS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel converter for noncontact charging with electromagnetic coupling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A DC-to-DC converter suitable for noncontact charging for the rechargeable cell using the electromagnetic coupling is presented. The circuit is of self-oscillated class C DC-to-DC converter. In this method, a class C converter is used for reducing the switching loss and the core loss of the transformer. The oscillating condition as a class C converter is automatically adjusted by a simple bias circuit which is made of a diode and a resistor. The zero voltage switching is realized by a resonance of the parasitic parameters of the transformer. Through electromagnetic coupling using this class C converter, we have obtained a noncontact type battery charger of 90% efficiency, under the input and output voltages and output power are 140 V, 12 V and 5 W respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Silicon component development and experimentation for primary protection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Primary protection in telecommunication network equipment makes use of gas tube discharge elements but, due to many disadvantages, the authors have examined the capability of silicon products. Existing product studies, the definition of the need, experimentation and validation of developed components as possible developments are part of this presentation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protection for switching systems: lightning, power grid, EMC, NEMP and related phenomena
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Like all telecommunication systems, switching systems must be designed to provide reasonable quality of service in an interference-producing electromagnetic environment, and at the same time limit the extent of any electromagnetic interference which they may generate. This paper summarizes the strategy of FRANCE TELECOM and its suppliers while placing it into an international context. In particular, it emphasizes the specific measures taken both in researching electromagnetic interference and in verifying the principles and rules applied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Heuristic method for auditing an electric power facility
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The calculation of the reliability of an electric-power facility by mean time between failures (MTBF) or failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) methods is extensive and expensive. A heuristic method is proposed in which one-or-more electric-power facilities are compared with an ideal system for that facility. A scoring method for the features of the ideal system provides a numerical rating for each alternative.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of a double-rectifier system using multilevel-voltage source diode rectifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Double-rectifier systems with novel modified diode bridge circuits are proposed. Although a conventional double rectifier system can produce 12-step input voltage waveforms, the proposed double rectifier system can produce 24-step or quasi 36-step input voltage waveforms. Total harmonic distortion of input voltages decrease to 10.67% in a single-rectifier system and to 5.12% in a double-rectifier system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of the response of a telecommunication building to a direct or distant lightning stroke
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents the main results of artificially triggered lightning experiments conducted in Saint Privat d'Allier to evaluate the effects of electromagnetic interferences on telecommunications systems. The authors emphasize the diversion of the currents and voltages induced on the different accesses of the building by a direct or a distant lightning stroke.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse hardening of power stations (generating sets). Methodology and industrial consequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The installation of electrical equipment with sensitive electronic devices in a severe electromagnetic environment, requires the implementation of particular protection. This article presents the methodological approach used in the frame of power stations hardening to high altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HA-NEMP) for a distributed protection. The article shows that this method allows optimization of the protection used while taking into account the notions of maintenance and cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Zero current switching high frequency inverter and converter utilized overlapping commutation mode in constant frequency power control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The principle of a constant frequency power control (CFPC) by phase difference regulation of the gate triggering pulse in the half bridge high frequency inverter (HBHF-INV) and high frequency link DC-DC converter (HFL DC-DC CONV) is proposed. The zero current switching (ZCS) techniques utilizing the overlapping commutation phenomena in the HBHF-INV and HFL DC-DC CONV are clarified. The characteristics of the CFPC with ZCS operation are numerically analyzed in association with normalized frequency and load.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a lead-acid battery for photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Reliable and cost efficient energy generation for remote telecommunication sites using engine generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the fundamentals of designing and implementing an engine generator-based primary energy system for remote telecommunication sites where key elements of the system's success are low maintenance, high reliability, and low operational cost with the lowest initial financial investment. The success of an environmentally uncontrolled cyclic prime power application, such as the one mentioned, has pushed both the monitoring and control technologies as well as the valve regulated batteries to their technological limits. By properly matching these technologies, a prime energy system can be implemented at a remote telecommunication site to meet the continuous energy demands while only running a fraction of a 24-hour period, thus providing longer engine service life and reduced operational costs. Combining remote monitoring features with this sort of system configuration has reduced power outages and has transformed reactive service emergencies into proactive system maintenance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short circuit current test results on AT&T round cells at different temperatures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The magnitude of short circuit battery currents is an important factor in designing DC systems including protective devices such as fuses and circuit breakers in standby power systems. Since the operating temperature of stationary batteries may fluctuate, it is also necessary to know the short circuit current at different temperatures. Currents close to short circuit were experimentally measured on three different types and sizes of AT&T Lineage 2000 Round Cells at room temperature and also at an elevated temperature, and the short circuit currents were then calculated. Short circuit currents were also calculated from the internal resistance of the batteries and compared with the experimental values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solar generators performance under high temperature
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The photovoltaic solar generators are today used for large numbers of telecommunication equipment in remote areas. The temperatures to which the solar modules are subject can become quite high. What is the solar cells and modules performance, and above all, what are the photovoltaic generator performance and the battery state of charge in such conditions? The instantaneous and continuous testing of the involved parameters enables the user to keep the solar generators in good working order under such conditions. The author discusses the temperature effects on the conversion efficiency and other parameters, and the economic implications of this.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power supply for the future Lebanese telecommunication network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: After 16 years of war, the Lebanese telecommunication network is badly destroyed. The rehabilitation/extension of this network is starting. The rehabilitation of around 100 power supply plants and the implementation of around 160 new power supply plants is planned. After a quick presentation of the actual and future Lebanese network, the authors describe the main constraints in the field of energy for the telecommunication. Afterwards some orientations for the future implementation of new power supply plants are proposed. The study of the Lebanese case can be extended to several countries in the world were similar constraints can be found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 20 years of experience with closed cycle vapor turbogenerators in extreme Arctic environment in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: One of the most severe problems confronting telecommunication projects in extreme Arctic environment conditions, with temperatures as low as -60/spl deg/C, is the supply of continuous, reliable remote power for unattended microwave repeater stations that in many cases cannot be reached by maintenance technicians for months at a time. Another important problem in such projects is that the telecommunications equipment must be kept at temperatures between 0/spl deg/C and +45/spl deg/C in order to ensure correct electronics operation. The use of specially designed, Arctic type, closed cycle vapor turbogenerators (CCVTs) and their associated nonelectric heating systems in Arctic telecommunication systems has solved both problems: reliable remote power in the range of 400 to 2000 Watts is provided and required temperature ranges in equipment shelters are maintained, assuring correct operation of sensitive electronics. The paper which follows describes the experience accumulated over the last 20 years in projects using CCVT's and associated heating systems in Russia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overvoltage and overcurrent protection of line interface maintaining high balance to earth
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the the overvoltage and overcurrent protection of a line interface between a two pair subscriber line and a telephone exchange. The interface provides conversion from two wire to four wire and may be used for analog and or digital signals. This new concept allows the use of components with reduced power ratings. Therefore less voluminous and less expensive components can be utilized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Turbo-alternators: a high-availability backup source of energy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Telecommunication systems require high availability of primary backup power supplies, consisting of generators intended to secure the system against failures of the public mains. In the context of a national program of refurbishment, France Telecom has developed new generators consisting of turbo-alternators designed with a single objective in mind: availability. The authors describe the architecture of a turbo-alternator based power system and its performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cogeneration systems using a diesel engine-generator for telecommunications power plants
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: NTT has been carrying out a "total power up" (TPU) campaign since 1987. The objective of the "TPU" campaign is to ensure profits by increasing revenues and reducing expenses. The introduction of cogeneration systems has been an effective part of the TPU campaign. As pilot plants, NTT introduced a cogeneration system using a diesel engine-generator into the Okayama Network Center in 1989, and a gas engine-generator system into the Osaka Network Center in 1990. The authors describe how full-scale introduction based upon these operation results has begun, and cogeneration systems using a diesel engine-generator have been introduced into the Sendai-tsutsujigaoka Branch Office and Tomakomai Branch Office in 1993.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of equipment and telecommunications networks in Europe
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Of the three fast-growing fields which emerged from electronics-telecommunications, data processing and media-telecommunications is the one now playing the strongest unifying role in Europe. Telecommunications are in fact the technical basis of communication in the widest sense including: voice; text; data; and video transmission. Continuous development in telecommunications is primarily the result of two driving forces: user needs; and technical advances in equipment. When comparing Eastern and Western Europe, the social and economic impact of telecommunications stands out clearly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Refitting a major microwave radio system with photovoltaic power supplies-four years later-lessons learned
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: At INTELEC'89, Kenney, Whittall and Larocque presented a paper on the planning and implementation aspects of replacing fuel dependent turbo-electric generating units by photovoltaic power supplies on a major microwave system in Africa. The present paper documents lessons learned during four years of operation and maintenance since the last paper. The major assumptions of the design were essentially correct. However, a number of design adjustments are recommended. Information and recommendations regarding sizing, type and life of batteries as well as specific gravity are presented. Modifications to the controllers are described. The document provides statistical and other information concerning the impact of the conversion program on maintenance and service reliability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety against fire risks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The risk of fire is an important and permanent potential risk for a telecommunications operator. This risk requires a coherent policy of safety and security, the main element of which is automatic fire detection. Recent changes of organisation and development of equipment and services in this field of activity have involved an evolution of this risk; increases of the fire and smoke potentials and a necessity to have the most reliable security equipment. Here, a complementary system of detection is described. It is a high sensitivity system, allowing very early alarm. It is considered as a technical alarm for technical staff in charge of the working and maintenance of telecommunications equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New products and technologies to comply with the Montreal Protocol
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: CFCs 11 and 12 have been successfully used in large centrifugal chillers for more than 50 years. The Montreal Protocol has banned the use of CFCs, necessitating the development of new products and technologies using the replacements R-123 and R-134a. These new refrigerants are available in new equipment as well as for use in converting existing CFC 11 and 12 equipment. Here, the author describes how replacement, conversion, and containment are the three primary alternatives for the equipment owner who is facing dwindling supplies of CFCs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer based evaluation of battery capacity tests
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The fully charged state and the ageing process of stationary batteries cannot be followed easily. The most effective method is the capacity test, which gives an exact result about the condition of battery cells. However, these results can depend on people who do the measuring. The evaluation of several different discharge processes are very hard because of the large amount of data. This paper introduces a computer-aided battery capacity test evaluation procedure which gives well ordered data sheets, shows the selected values in diagrams, calculates the partial and final results in the same way, so the results of different measuring series will be comparable. The program is able to compare the results of annual capacity tests and gives a good view about the expectable future behavior trend of the examined batteries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passive temperature regulation of outdoor cabinets and shelters using pure water and night sky radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Passive air conditioning of outdoor cabinets and shelters has been performed for many years. Heat from the equipment is stored in a thermal mass as latent heat then disposed of through a heat exchanger to the relatively cool night air. During the hottest time of the year, sky temperature is often at least 15/spl deg/C below ambient, allowing 60 watts/M/sup 2/ to radiate outward even after the radiator has cooled to ambient temperature. To explore night sky radiation the radiator is larger than the shelter roof, giving both day time shade and extra night cooling. The water is its own thermostat because it ceases to flow by convection to the radiator at 4/spl deg/C, the temperature of maximum density. Water's high (80 cal/gram) heat of fusion makes it the perfect medium for storing heat to prevent cabinets from cooling below 0/spl deg/C. All components must be freeze tolerant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Earthing: parts, performances, cabling and impacts on electronic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Electronic systems, according to their manufacturers, require a very good "earth electrode". To demonstrate that earthing is not the good solution, but grounding is necessary for the electronics, the authors first study the use of earth electrodes, from "security" to "working". In this use, they define the absolute necessity of a equipotential grounding network. They present a measure of the earthing resistance and present results of experimental measures of earthing impedance as a function of frequency. Finally, they demonstrate the absolute impracticality (always as a function of frequency) of shielded groundings or earthings. They also give simple advices aimed at improving the equipotentiality of electronic systems grounding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal control of equipment enclosures-design strategies for enhanced reliability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Thermal control of electronic equipment enclosures within specified temperature limits is vital to maintain an acceptable level of communication system reliability. The paper introduces novel design strategies using precooled concrete of the building structure integrated with phase change material ("PCM") thermal storage and the vacuum panel heat exchanger("VPHE") to protect equipment enclosures from excessive temperature rise in times of loss of the normal cooling system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system for power systems maintenance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: When power equipment fails, maintenance personnel have traditionally had to investigate and repair the equipment by using information supplied by supervision and control systems, specified in manuals, or gained through personal experience. To enable maintenance personnel to respond more quickly and accurately, the authors have developed an expert system (called ALICE-ES), that provides diagnostic expert know-how and emergency procedures arranged in knowledge bases. These knowledge bases can be used to visually display optimal resolution procedures. ALICE-ES also has a friendly human-machine interface, offering features like full mouse-click operation and help functions. This paper describes the configuration, the functions, and the system technology of ALICE-ES.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two wire automatic remote sensing and evaluation systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The Two Wire Automatic Remote Sensing and Evaluation System (TWARSES) automatically transmits and evaluates information (data) from remote sensors on a common two wires bus. In addition, the system presents automatic evaluation and alarms which provide both location data and sensor readout data of the monitored area. This system is a stand-alone modular system in which a common two wire line installed bow-to-stern and top-to-bottom contacts, integrates, evaluates, and powers most sensors. The United States Navy uses this system to provide safety and survivability by monitoring environmental gases, liquid levels, power, temperature, and humidity levels on ships and in office buildings. The system automatically polls all sensor transponders who first energized, then evaluates the output of each sensor against preset limits. The internal program is designed so that any sensor can have limits listed and the printout and alarm will be initiated by an out-of-limit condition. This system permits both data evaluation, printed listings, recorded cards and displays to be done automatically, with alarms on all types of specific conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Elements for a unified approach to system protection against broadband electromagnetic disturbances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Developments over the past few years involve: design of electronic systems with intensive use of VLSI, but more sensitive to electromagnetic disturbance; use of composite materials to replace metals, due to their mechanical strength and lightweight but allowing greater field penetration given their lower shielding efficiency; and desire for electronic systems whose performance is not affected by an ever increasing range of electromagnetic environments covering a continuous frequency range from a few kilohertz to several tens of gigahertz. In view of these simultaneous constraints, the authors have introduced elements for a protection methodology and a principle for hardening systems against a set of broadband electromagnetic disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switch transitions in the soft-switching full-bridge PWM phase-shift DC/DC converter: analysis and improvements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An analysis is presented for determining the commutating energy available for the clocked or passive-to-active leg of a full-bridge soft-switching power converter with an external commutating aid, as a function of the load current. It is shown that by properly choosing the values of the circuit inductances, soft switching can be achieved over a wide range of load current without a significant penalty in conduction loss. The currents in the clamp diodes of the commutating aid depend on the location of the commutating inductor. If the inductor is connected between the passive-to-active leg and the transformer, excess current circulates in the clamp diodes, leading to switching losses and potential failure of the diodes. The excess current is not present if the commutating inductor is connected between the active-to-passive leg and the transformer. The predictions of analysis are verified by computer simulation and by experimental results taken from a 3 kW converter with 200 kHz clock frequency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Soft-switched DC/DC converter with PWM control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper, a soft-switched power converter with two variations is discussed. An asymmetrical PWM control scheme is used to control the power converter under constant switching frequency operation. The modes of operation for both variations are discussed. The DC characteristics which can be used in design of the converters are also presented. Two 50 W converters were built to verify the characteristics of the converters. Due to the zero voltage switching (ZVS) operation of the switches and low device voltage and current stresses, the converters have high full load and partial load efficiencies. They are potential candidates for high efficiency, high density power supply applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Input current shaping and regulation of multiple outputs in a single isolated converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Input current shaping and wide bandwidth regulation of multiple outputs is demonstrated in a single power stage. These isolated capacitive idling converters, when operated in discontinuous inductor current mode (DICM) on the primary side, perform the input current shaping automatically, i.e. without the input current feedback loop. Consequently, the high power factor performance is obtained without any penalty in complexity, cost and efficiency of the converter. Moreover, due to the internal energy storage and presence of one secondary-side active switch for each output, the capacitive idling converters provide full regulation and short-circuit protection of all outputs, and eliminate the need to cross isolation barrier in the feedback path.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel single-switch three-phase AC/DC buck-boost converter with high-quality input current waveforms and isolated DC output
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new three-phase single-switch AC-DC flyback power converter system is presented. The system operates in the discontinuous mode. The simple structure of its power and control circuit, low mains current distortion and resistive fundamental behavior as well as the high-frequency isolation of the controlled output voltage are pointed out. Besides the analysis of the stationary operating behavior the dependencies of the peak values, average values and RMS values of the device currents and of the maximum blocking voltages across the power electronic devices on the circuit parameters are given as analytic approximations. The theoretical analysis is verified by digital simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aging effects in valve-regulated lead-acid batteries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Hydrogen evolution at the negative electrode and corrosion of the positive grid are unavoidable secondary reactions in lead-acid batteries. Both cause water loss, that gradually changes the cell balance in valve-regulated types, because it cannot be compensated for by refilling. Thus, charge and discharge behaviour of valve-regulated Pb-acid batteries gradually changes with service life. The impact of water loss on discharge behaviour is different between batteries based on absorbent-glass-mat separators and those with gelled electrolyte. The authors describe how this has been elucidated with batteries that had lost a considerable amount of water by special pretreatment. Both effects can, at least partly, be explained by the pore structure of the medium between the electrodes. The pore sizes in absorbent-glass-mat separators are coarse compared to those of the active material or both electrodes. So, capillary forces of the active material are higher, and water loss occurs mainly at the expense of the water content in the separator. In gelled electrolyte, a real pore structure cannot be ascertained by direct measurement but the electrolyte behaves in the same way as in a felt with a pore system one order of magnitude finer than that of the absorbent-glass-mat separator. Thus, 'capillary competition' between active material and immobilized electrolyte are less significant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field and laboratory studies to assess the state of health of valve-regulated lead acid and other battery technologies using conductance testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper demonstrates the high correlation of capacity and conductance on hundreds of cells in telecommunication, UPS, railroad signalling and other usages. It confirms the premature capacity loss of valve regulated lead acid (VRLA) cells reported previously and provides information on failure modes via post mortem tear-down of some of the defective cells. Further, it extends the correlation of conductance and capacity to flooded lead acid cells and provides preliminary data of capacity conductance correlation with flooded nickel cadmium (Ni-Cd) batteries. It also introduces the results of techniques of noise suppression to allow online conductance measurements to be made on the batteries without interruption while the batteries continue in service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TENOR: power supply with a single AC/DC conversion stage and distributed energy storage adapted for telecommunication and computing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents the evolution of the energy power supply of telecommunication systems. The exchange and transmission equipment, centralized or distributed, need less and less power. The power is essentially used under electronic voltage (80 % under 5 V and 3 V for new technologies and some 12 V). Only 20 % of the power is delivered under 54 V for the remote power supply of the subscriber line. This voltage is no longer useful for the GSM radio network and FTTC optical network. Until now, the standardized voltage interface 48 V or 60 V remains the reference for telecommunication equipment. This voltage is supplied by decentralized DC cabinets having 1 hour autonomy, installed near the system or even integrated in the system itself. These cabinets are powered by the high availability GEODE AC source under 3 phase AC 400 V voltage of the public mains. Associated computers for complementary services, are powered by UPS providing an autonomy of 10 to 15 min. The standardized interface with the equipment is in this case the single phase public AC mains 230 V voltage. So, in the same centers, two uninterrupted power sources, DC 48 V and AC 230 V, run together with two standardized voltage interfaces, DC and AC. The TENOR project's aim is the unification of these two power supply methods with a single AC interface applicable to any size of installation. This result can be achieved through the new concept of distributed energy storage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of AC impedance/conductance and DC resistance for determining the reliability of VRLA battery systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The reliability of valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA) cells has been an issue in the light of the relative immaturity of this technology. AC impedance/conductance is being promoted as a means of determining their 'state of health', as signified by their ability to perform electrically to end of life. Claims have been made that the higher the conductance, or the lower the impedance, the better the battery. The authors' efforts have focussed on evaluating this and similar techniques towards the goal of determining VRLA battery performance and reliability. Impedance and conductance measurements were made on large number of VRLA cells and batteries in the size range of 25 to over 2000 Ah, using several different commercially available meters. Data on new as well as naturally and artificially aged cells and batteries are discussed as are extended performance data and teardown analysis of cells at end of life. Results from DC resistance, measured by a voltage-relaxation technique, are also compared and correlated with that from impedance/conductance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The maturing of a valve regulated (VRLA) battery technology: ten years of experience
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new era in telecommunications standby power started 10 years ago with the advent of valve regulated lead acid (VRLA) batteries in capacities ranging from 100 to 1000 Ah. Since then, the telecommunications industry, its services, telecom equipment and batteries supporting this equipment have undergone a major evolution. Industry-wide. VRLA batteries' share of annual battery sales have increased from zero to 60%. Reduced maintenance requirements, lighter weight, reduced footprint and volume, fewer environmental considerations, and lower installation and operating costs are features which make these batteries popular. As with any evolving technology, both users and suppliers have encountered obstacles and roadblocks. To be sure, manufacturers and users have made mistakes in adopting this new technology. However, as advancements in VRLA technology are made, the telecommunications industry will be able to provide services that would not have been possible without VRLA batteries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterisation of cross regulation in DC-DC converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A novel theoretical framework is presented for quantifying all types of regulation-line, load and cross regulation-in any N-port DC-DC power converter, under a linear approximation. The equations have been embodied in a SPICE macromodel, which has been verified experimentally. This is believed to be the first general theory of cross regulation in DC-DC power converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical considerations using distributed power modules in decentralized power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The design of modern decentralized power systems in telecommunication applications are normally realized by using distributed DC/DC power modules. Power modules are usually characterized by high switching frequencies which enables the use of small ferrite magnetics and ceramic capacitors to enhance the reliability, the power density and the possibility of live insertion, all desired features in new power system designs. However, to utilize the advantages of power modules there are a number of considerations to be made in the design. This paper addresses these considerations by focusing on systems with an average power dissipation of <10 W/board, in free convection cooled cabinets, and <80 W/board, in forced convection cooled cabinets of commonly used mechanical sizes and designs for telecommunication equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Battery diagnostics and performance prediction: computational vs. expert system based approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper, two methods for battery field diagnostics and performance prediction are discussed. The former is a computational method which employs the relationships between the internal state indicators of a cell and the most significant influencing factors (e.g., temperature, technology, electrolyte density, age, work cycle). The latter uses artificial intelligence techniques based on rules developed from the expertise of specialists. The two methods are compared with respect to stationary batteries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fan-cooled power systems for telecom applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Introduction of fan-cooled rectifiers into large centralized telecommunication power supply systems is a logical consequence of continuing evolution of general environment to world-wide politics, economy and industry. The paper emphasises that forced cooling does not impair the system availability. The means to achieve this is redundancy, load sharing and fan supervision. Controllers with self-diagnosis and state-of-the-system-monitoring routines enhance user-friendliness and decrease operation expenses. The initial acquisition costs are kept low by the modular concept allowing the plant to grow as the load demand increases. Modularity also permits component cost reduction by standardization and provides flexibility in realizing systems meeting different local specifications and requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Telephone exchange primary protection developments towards silicon structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: For the past few years, protection systems have been developing towards silicon components. This tendency, which has already been well established for secondary protection is also being applied to primary protection. Initially, the idea was to replace gas discharge arresters. However, the potential characteristics of silicon should be able to enrich this function by generating structures which, though monolithic, will integrate an increasing number of diagnostic functions, allowing the protection product to self-adapt to the instantaneous configuration of the circuit. The authors describe the various options which should emerge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Research and industrial development of telecommunications in South East Asia: Indonesian experience
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Intelec 93: 15th International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper focuses on a discussion of research and development policies and activities in Indonesia's telecommunications industry where P.T. Telkom (the state enterprise for domestic telecommunications) holds a leading role. This paper also discusses research and development management problems of human resources, funding and the necessity to have a long term research and development vision and mission. Finally, the paper concludes that better international cooperation is needed to improve the transfer of technology and telecommunication development in developing countries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
